textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 science · The World of Metals and Non-metals · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Many metals are shiny when their surfaces are clean. They often conduct heat and electricity well. Other properties, such as hardness, vary from metal to metal.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Many metals are shiny when their surfaces are clean. They often conduct heat and electricity well. Other properties, such as hardness, vary from metal to metal.
beats.speakEn: Many metals are shiny when their surfaces are clean. They often conduct heat and electricity well. Other properties, such as hardness, vary from metal to metal.

beats.en: Many solid non-metals are brittle and conduct electricity poorly. Some non-metals, such as oxygen, are gases at room temperature. Oxygen and nitrogen are gaseous non-metals at room temperature.
beats.speakEn: Many solid non-metals are brittle and conduct electricity poorly. Some non-metals, such as oxygen, are gases at room temperature. Oxygen and nitrogen are gaseous non-metals at room temperature.

type: Key Concept: Many metals are shiny when their surfaces are clean.
Rule: Many solid non-metals are brittle and conduct electricity poorly.

textbookBox.concept: Many metals form oxides when they react with oxygen. Rusting is a specific change in iron or steel that requires oxygen and moisture.

beats.en: Many metals form oxides when they react with oxygen. Rusting is a specific change in iron or steel that requires oxygen and moisture. Some metals can release hydrogen when they react with certain acids.
beats.speakEn: Many metals form oxides when they react with oxygen. Rusting is a specific change in iron or steel that requires oxygen and moisture. Some metals can release hydrogen when they react with certain acids.

beats.en: Copper is used in wires, iron and its alloys in many tools, aluminium in foil and gold in some jewellery. These uses depend on a combination of properties.
